title: Chinese AI companies buy 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs in a single year, report claims
source_used: Tom's Hardware, relaying a Financial Times report
key_facts: The Financial Times reports that Chinese tech companies bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs to plug gaps in AI computing power; it cites industry insiders.

China's domestic AI chip production has doubled this year but cannot keep up: about 3.5 million chips expected domestically against demand that far exceeds 5 million, a shortfall of nearly 1.5 million.
The chips are mostly Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000D, RTX Pro 5000 and RTX 5090, which comply with US export controls and are repurposed for AI.
These Blackwell chips cannot match Huawei's Ascend 910C but are useful for simpler AI workloads such as prefilling.
Demand is also driven by Nvidia's CUDA software, which remains more favoured than Huawei's CANN.
Tom's Hardware adds that the RTX 5090 (list price USD 1,999) is now found at only about three third-party resellers for at least USD 7,199.
quote_evidence: Chinese tech companies have bought more than 1 million Nvidia gaming and workstation GPUs to plug gaps in demand for AI computing power, Financial Times reports.
The report cites a shortfall of nearly 1.5 million chips, with only 3.5 million expected to be manufactured domestically while demand "far exceeds" 5 million.
The report cites industry insiders who claim the buying spree highlights an ongoing and significant reliance on U.S. AI hardware, despite a burgeoning homegrown market.
why_it_matters_hint: China still leans on US-designed chips for AI, and the demand is squeezing the gaming graphics card market.
event_date: 13 Oct 2026 (Tom's Hardware report; date of the FT report not stated)
notes: Tom's Hardware page text read; the Financial Times original was not opened (paywalled). Figures come from unnamed industry insiders in one newspaper report.
